comment.narrative: 12-07-2022: After identifying professional tasks for four different profiles (TVET technical-instructor, TVET trainer, TVET developer and TVET manager) assessments and learning tasks are developed for each of these professional tasks. Each professional task representing one module. It was agreed to start piloting the profile of technical-instructor and trainer. At KTTC the profile of technical-instructor and trainer are both part of a separate one year study programme. At Egerton University and Bukura Agricultural College the profile of technical-instructor will be part of a three year diploma programme. And at Egerton University the profile of trainer will be part of a four year bachelor programme. In all curricula a new module on gender and inclusiveness is developed and introduced in the curricula. During the MTR process (report is annexed) it became evident that this is a very innovative approach which has high potential to be rolled-out in the whole TVET sector (not only agriculture). Egerton has chosen to prepare also one TVET trainer course and a TVET teacher post graduate course that will be implemented once Egerton University has been accredited as TVET institute. This can be considered as a spin-off of this Nuffic-project, although these curricula will not be piloted during the project period.

24-02-2021: Is in process in two ways: A DACUM process is being done that will deliver the occupational profiles (OP), standards (OS) and curricula as required by CDACC/TVETA in the Kenyan system. The project developed OP/OS for TVET instructor and OP/OS for TVET Manager-developer. CDACC is actively involved. Another process being enhanced, is the design of professional task, assessment criteria, learning outcomes and teaching-learning materials. Parallel the traineeship programme is being revised to be improved (year 2). As a result, 4 curricula are in process of being revised and approved. For the development of curricula, 21 professional tasks have been selected. Professional tasks for technical-instructor, trainer, developer and manager. The selected professional tasks are used for revision of four curricula. Two at KTTC: for technical-instructor and for trainer both one year programmes. At Egerton University a two programme’s and a 4 years programme for trainers.

25-09-2023: Four curricula and occupational profiles (OP) and standards (OS) have been developed for TVET Technical instructor, TVET Trainer, TVET Manager and TVET Developer using DACUM procedures. In addition, professional tasks, assessments, learning tasks and teaching-learning materials have been developed for the TVET Technical trainer and TVET Trainer programmes. These programmes are also being implemented at Egerton University, KTTC and Bukura Agricultural College. At KTTC the developed programme is not only used for the regular intake but also for the students following the in-service program. Since the developed programmes are piloted extensively with different cohorts of students the lessons learned could be used to modify and further improve the modules. The internship programme is revised and improved resulting in instructions and assignments for two Field Attachments and two Teaching Practices each with their own objectives and assignments. To enhance online learning and communication between students and lecturers and coaches during the internship periods the portfolio’s with instructions and assignments are made online available by using the existing learning platforms at the respective institutes, also called the CoachingApp since during the internship period the students have access to the information and can communicate with peers and coaches by smartphone as well. A training for workplace coaches has been developed. After the initial training has been piloted in a life mode the training was transferred to an online platform to provide online access and support time and place independent training of workplace coaches. As a joint venture between two OKP-KEN projects, a Climate Smart Dairy Course was developed. TVETA also developed the training standards for TVET Manager and TVET Developer, which have been validated by KEBS. Gender and inclusion are integrated across the standards, aligned to prevailing Disability laws and policies.

title.narrative: A.E.1. Number of (knowledge) institutions supported directly

comment.narrative: 07-09-2021: The project started the process of improving the curricula of Egerton University and KTTC. Professional tasks, assessment criteria and learning tasks have been developed. An inventory of traineeship programmes and experiences has been concluded. TVET institutes like Latia, Bukura and DTI participated actively in these processes. Each project partner revised critically their existing partnerships and is in process of connecting with new partners. TVETA is coordinating the project activities in a very effective way.

25-09-2023: Throughout the entire duration of the project TVETA, Egerton University, KTTC as well as Bukura Agricultural College, Latia Resource Center and DTI have been supported. Egerton University, KTTC and Bukura Agricultural College were able to benefit from all project components, including the revised curricula, teacher training, the G&I modules, improved partnerships, quality assurance mechanisms and the TVET Partnership Platform and Coaching App. Latia and DTI participated in and contributed to most of the project activities. The investment budget has been used to improve the facilities for practical teaching and learning in 5 TVET institutions and the TVET Authority has been supported to enhance effective and efficient regulator tasks as part of its mandate.

24-02-2021: Supported by the OKP project, 2 DACUM based occupational profiles and standards for TVET instructor and TVET Manager-developer are being prepared and will be published in year 2. These will be based on the CDACC, KNQA and CBET requirements, having been validated by 3 TVET institutions and industry if situation regarding Covid-19 will allow this.

25-09-2023: • OP, OS, curricula and learning guides and teacher instructions for TVET Technical instructor (level 5) • OP, OS, curricula and learning guides and teacher instructions for TVET Trainer (level 6) • OP, OS, curricula for TVET Manager (level 8) • OP, OS and curricula for TVET Developer (level 8) • Four manuals with instructions for internships (Teaching Practice I and II and Field Attachment I and II); as part of the Coaching App • Training for workplace coaches with six modules; online training • G&I module • Quality assurance in workplace-based technical and vocational education and training and industrial attachments in a perspective of the qualifications framework; The prospectus (scientific publication). Student instructions are described in learning guides. One learning guide for each module containing the assessment, learning tasks and an overview of subjects for theory and practical’s. Each module also is supported with a teacher guide. For each of the modules of the programme of TVET Technical instructor (7) and TVET Trainer (6) these learning guides and teaching guides have been prepared and revised and finalised during the piloting period at the different institutes. Besides these learning and teaching guides also the instructions for four different internships are developed. Two for the Field Attachment (I and II) and two for the Teaching Practice (I and II). These instructions are part of the coaching platform or Coaching App for guidance of the different internships. This coaching platform is made available in Moodle which also can be used by using a smartphone. The instructions are piloted and revised and finalised based on experiences at the different institutes.

25-09-2023: The project innovations addressed the teaching and learning approaches used so far in ATVET teacher training in Kenya. The new approach is based on selecting professional tasks of an agricultural TVET Technical instructor and TVET Trainer as the basis for the curricula. Developed modules are based on these professional tasks and assessments are constructed to test students ability to perform those professional tasks. Learning tasks are designed to offer students the possibility to practice the professional tasks to gain routine and professional task descriptions are used to decide about relevant theory to be thought and skills to be trained during practical’s. Another innovation consists of the improvement of the traineeship programme at both industry and TVET institutes. By making a distinction between Field attachment (learning experience in the agricultural sector at different levels in the value chain) and Teaching practice (to gain practical experience in teaching and training activities in an educational context. Aiming at improving students knowledge of agricultural practices and sector at one hand and providing student the opportunity to gain teaching experience already at an early stage at the other hand. Other relevant innovations include the online Partnership platform and the CoachingApp. This platform and App has been installed and rolled out at KTTC, Egerton University, Bukura Agricultural College and also The Eldoret National Polytechnic (partner in OKP–KEN-104647). The platform and App contributes significantly to the improvement of internship programmes at the different TVET Institutions. In the last project year the training for workplace coaches was transferred to on online platform to make time and place independent training of workplace coaches possible. title.narrative: A.S.3. Number of students performing an internship or practical work

comment.narrative: 30 ATVET trainers students perform a traineeship

12-07-2022: The revision of the internship programmes of Egerton University and KTTC in relation to the teacher training programmes is taking place. In the educational programmes of these institutes two internships related to Teaching practice are planned. During these internships students will practice educational activities at TVET institutes. For the pilot phase this will take place at Latia, DTI and Bukura Agricultural College. Besides the two Teaching practices (traineeship periods), KTTC students will execute one field attachment and Egerton University will execute two field attachments (industry or NGOs) with the objective to gain knowledge and skills in relation to the agricultural sector. For each of these traineeships specific assignments have been developed. Both institutes are using Moodle as education learning management system. The Moodle platform will be used to provide student instructions related to the activities they need to perform during the internships. The platform will also be used by students to upload the results of their assignments such as video and audio materials, as well as documents. This will enable internship coaches and assessors to frequently guide and evaluate students online while reducing the need to visit students during their internship. Moodle is available as an app on smartphones which will stimulate the use of the educational platform when the student is in the field. The development of a training programme for traineeship and workplace coaches is in progress. Target groups for this training are the coaches of the ‘home institutes’ like KTTC and Egerton University, coaches of the ‘receiving institutes’ like DTI, Latia and Bukura Agricultural College and workplace coaches of agricultural companies and organisations which provide internships for field attachments.

24-02-2021: The improvement of the existing traineeship and industrial attachment programmes is in process. A mobile phone app for ATVET teacher training coaching processes will be developed to make coaching more useful and effective as part of the learning and teaching process. The project aimed at having 268 students performing an (improved) internship but taking into account the limitations imposed by Covid-19 we will monitor if this really will be feasible within the time-span of the project.

25-09-2023: Objectives and instructions for four different internship programmes (Field Attachment I and II and Field Attachment I and II) were developed and as portfolio added to the Coaching App. KTTC piloted the Teaching practice with respectively 84, 94, 127 and 94 students. And in addition also 66 in-service students (incl. 5 of project partner Latia) used the portfolio. Another 74 students are expected to finish their Teaching practice before July ’24. The portfolio for the Field attachment was piloted with respectively 117 and 94 students. And in addition 66 in-service (incl. 5 of Latia) students used the portfolio. Another 74 are expected to finish their Teaching practice before Nov ’23. Egerton University piloted the Teaching practice II with 30 students and a selection out of in total 160 students. The Field attachment II was piloted with 111 + 30 (out of 56) students. Bukura Agricultural College piloted the Teaching practice with 10 students.

title.narrative: A.O.7. % of women in management of faculty/department

comment.narrative: 24-02-2021: The project didn’t take specific actions, in activities enhanced so far by the project the participation of male and female is distributed equally. In specific G & I staff training planned in the project, a module on gender & inclusiveness learning and teaching processes will be prepared. Equal participation will be dealt with in this module.

25-09-2023: Female representation among management and teaching staff is fairly equal. During the coaching and backstopping special attention has been given to the institutional aspects of G&I in the ATVET-TT Institutes. With the implementation of the Guidelines for gender-responsive and inclusive ATVET the project has further embedded this within the institutions. At management level it can be note that for 2 years Egerton had a female Vice Chancellor although after finishing her term a male candidate was selected as successor. In Egerton University almost 50% of the management board members are female. In Bukura Agricultural College, the board consists of almost 50% of female members, while at the level of Directors 33% is female. In the KSTVET Governing Council almost 50% of the members are female.

comment.narrative: 24-02-2021: The project didn’t take specific actions, in activities enhanced so far by the project the participation of male and female is distributed equally. In specific G & I staff training planned in the project, a module on gender & inclusiveness learning and teaching processes will be prepared. Equal participation will be dealt with in this module.

25-09-2023: All project partner institutes apply gender inclusiveness and diversity policies, as such diversity is equally distributed. Gender committees are established and procedures against inequal treatment and harassment are in place. With the support of the project, a module on G & I is developed implemented and embedded at classroom level with explicitly supported by the management of all the institutes. Female representation among management and teaching staff is fairly equal although still less than 50%. During the coaching and backstopping special attention has been given to the institutional aspects of G&I in the ATVET-TT Institutes. With the implementation of the Guidelines for gender-responsive and inclusive ATVET the project has further embedded this within the institutions. Support activities like coaching and exchange of experiences have been enhanced. With that we can conclude that a gender-responsive and inclusive TVET in Kenya has been given a clear basis in the graduates of the Teacher Training programme are and will be new generation of ATVET teachers and managers. In 5 implementing Kenya partners around 40% of the teaching staff is female.

Nonetheless, KTTC embarked on a project to implement Moodle to support their teaching activities. The materials developed by the consortium are embedded in KTTC’s online learning environment (Moodle). Furthermore, the Moodle system will also be used for the mobile / web-based system to coach both workplace coaches (at the company), workplace supervisors (at the TVET institute) and the trainees. Initial development has been done, and each participating institute will provide their coaching framework allowing to incorporate and test the system accordingly. This will allow for better organization of student placements. The (online) partnership platform will also be linked to the quality standards for companies and TVET institutes hosting future trainees. These standards will be developed by the project in close cooperation with TVETA, the Institutes and private sector.

title.narrative: A.E.3. Number of staff that have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge and skills to develop and offer the revised/developed study programmes

comment.narrative: 12-07-2022: Online workshops have taken place to improve and develop curricula for TVET technical instructor, TVET trainer, TVET manager and TVET developer curricula as per the CBETA Standards and guidelines. The Occupational Standards(OS) and CBET documents as required in the Kenya TVET have been finalized. The first two sets have been approved by TVETA accordingly wherein assessments, assignments and teaching and learning materials (TLM) have been prepared and will be piloted with the support of project experts. Each participating institute (Egerton University, KTTC, Bukura Agricultural College, Latia, DTI, TVETA) was represented by a certain number of staff. On average 15 persons participated in the workshops. In each workshop more or less the same individuals participated, save for the validation workshops where new participants that are not normally involved for the drafting of the OS, the curriculum and the TLM are usually involved. As such the participants gained solid experience in CBET curriculum development. In the last two online workshops KTTC and Bukura Agricultural College brought additional colleagues to prepare them for the implementation of the newly developed CBET curriculum.

25-09-2023: 30 (10 F / 20 M) number of staff gained knowledge and skills to develop and offer revised study programs. This includes the dissemination in internally in each institute and the validation workshops for the Standard and guidelines on Traineeships/Field attachments, involving the ILO’s of each institute. Staff of the 5 TVET Institutions have been actively involved in the development of TVET Technical instructor, TVET Trainer, TVET Manager and TVET Developer curricula as well as learning guides and teacher instructions for TVET Technical instructor and TVET Trainer including assessments, learning tasks and teaching-learning materials including selected theory and practical’s to be performed by students. Furthermore, the G&I module and the specific training for the workplace coaches of companies and the educational institutes. • 15 (5 F/ 10 M) staff members participated in the various sessions of the DACUM process for the development of the TVET technical instructor, TVET trainer, TVET manager and TVET developer curricula. • 15 staff (6 F / 9 M) members of the involved institutes participated in the various curriculum development workshops to develop the assessments, learning tasks for the programme of TVET Technical instructor and TVET Trainer. And complementing it with selecting the appropriate theory and practical’s. • 31 (20 F / 11 M) staff members participated in the G&I module development process • 12 staff (3 F / 9 M) were prepared in the use of the Partnership platform and traineeship coaching App • 18 (5 F / 13 M) staff members participated in the online workplace coaches training development process In the last project year staff of Egerton University, KTTC and Bukura Agricultural College was actively guided in the implementation of the developed curricula. During the implementation also other colleagues of the respective institutes were involved.
